title: He Owned Two Pairs of Jeans… and a $3 Million Secret
yt_title: He Owned Two Pairs of Jeans… and a $3 Million Secret 🤫 #shorts
yt_description:
Dale Schroeder worked as a carpenter at the same Iowa company for 67 years. Work jeans on weekdays, church jeans on Sundays, one rusty Chevy truck. Nobody guessed he was rich.

Before he died in 2005, he told his lawyer he wanted to help kids go to college – and that he had saved just shy of $3 million. His money paid for 33 strangers from small-town Iowa to go to college, debt-free. Today they call themselves "Dale's Kids". His only request: pay it forward.

A true story. Sources: CBS News, KCCI, Wikipedia.

#unsungstories #truestory #kindness #payitforward #inspiration #shorts
script: In two thousand five, an Iowa carpenter died owning two pairs of jeans... and a secret nobody had guessed. Dale Schroeder worked at the same company for sixty-seven years. Work jeans on weekdays. Church jeans on Sundays. One rusty Chevy truck. Nobody in town thought he was rich. Then, near the end, Dale visited his lawyer. "I never got to go to college," he said. "I'd like to help kids go." "How much are we talking about, Dale?" "Oh... just shy of three million dollars." His lawyer nearly fell out of his chair. The money went to small-town kids who had the grades, but not the cash. One student. Ten. Twenty. Thirty-three. Doctors. Teachers. Therapists. No debt. They had never met him. Years later, they all gathered around the one thing he left behind... his old lunch box. Dale asked for only one thing in return. Not to pay him back. To pay it forward.
